neighbours.label: the journey/vehicle noun slot after light-verb 'took the' / 'made the' in a travel sentence (took the fast train, made the 30 minute drive, made the trek)
fire: After the wedding we took the fast train back to Osaka.
On Friday my brother made the 90 minute drive from Leeds to Hull.
Each August the family makes the trek out to the old farm in Montana.
Her grandparents took the night train from Prague to Budapest.
Last Sunday I made the three hour drive down to San Diego.
To save time, the students took the express train into Tokyo.
In March she made the long drive north to Inverness alone.
That evening we took the slow train along the coast to Genoa.
quiet: After the wedding our flight back to Osaka was delayed.
On Friday my brother drove ninety minutes from Leeds to Hull.
Each August the family hikes out to the old farm in Montana.
Her grandparents travelled overnight by rail from Prague to Budapest.
Last Sunday I was driving for three hours on my way to San Diego.
The express train into Tokyo was crowded with students.
In March she drove north to Inverness alone.
That evening a slow train carried us along the coast to Genoa.

notes: Probes: 'took the fast/night train' 0.92-0.93, 'made the N minute drive' 0.58-0.84, 'made the trek/trip' 0.45. Leaks to other objects of took/made the ('took the medicine' 0.38, 'made the cake' 0.35) and a bare subject 'The fast train' 0.28, so the light verb matters as much as the journey.
